newsitem.title: KENYA: Forty-one ships expected in Mombasa next 2 weeks.
newsitem.headline: Forty-one ships expected in Mombasa next 2 weeks.

text.p: A total of 41 ships carrying 121,724 tonnes of cargo will dock at the Port of Mombasa in the next two weeks and will load 28,726 tonnes of goods on their return journeys, the Kenya Ports Authority said.

A shipping report from the authority, issued on Thursday, showed the cargo due in included salt, fertiliser, new and used vehicles, crude and refined oil, liquefied petroleum gas (LPG), clinker, rice and steel.
The LPG was bought in Malaysia by local oil companies to back up erratic local supplies from the Kenya Oil Refinery. The 1,300 tonnes of LPG arrives on board the Cypriot registered MV Sandown.
MV Park Dream, which was scheduled to arrive on Monday with World Food Programme (WFP) wheat donated by the Netherlands government, will now dock on September 4.
Another WFP cargo of green peas donated by the Danish government for a programme in Uganda is due to arrive on August 31 on board MV City of Glasgow.
WFP will also bring in seed oil for the same programme on board MV Ensign. The cargo arrives on September 7.
There are seven empty conventional and container berths -- numbers 3, 8, 10, 11, 12, 14 and 16.
MV Mwenge is waiting midstream to load 1,000 tonnes of general cargo while MV Uhuru is waiting to load petroleum products.
